name: Act of March 2, 1889: the Pine Ridge reservation (Royce 700)
citation: Act of March 2, 1889, ch. 405, 25 Stat. 888 (in force by proclamation of February 10, 1890)
promises: The Act set apart for the Indians receiving rations at the Pine Ridge agency the lands between the 103rd meridian, the South Fork of the Cheyenne, the White River and the Nebraska line, plus a tract in Nebraska (Royce).

The Act of March 2, 1889 divided the Great Sioux Reservation into separate reservations; section 21 opened the rest to sale for the benefit of the Sioux, and section 19 kept in force all provisions of the 1868 treaty and the 1877 agreement not in conflict with it (Court of Claims, 105 Ct. Cl. 725).
today: In 1946 the Court of Claims allowed nothing on the Pine Ridge claims (case C-531 (20)): it held that tribal funds spent on White River bridges under an Act of 1920 were not recoverable; the ration-charge claim was not made for Pine Ridge funds (105 Ct. Cl. 725). The Oglala Sioux Tribe says the Pine Ridge reservation was established in 1889 out of the reduced Great Sioux Reservation.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says the Great Sioux Reservation of the 1868 treaty was later reduced to five reservations, Pine Ridge among them in 1889, and that the loss of land including the Black Hills remains in contention.

sources.title: Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report, Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 932, Pine Ridge Sioux entry
Sioux Tribe of Indians v. United States, 105 Ct. Cl. 725 (1946), Nos. C-531 (18) to (24)
sources.publisher: Caselaw Access Project, Harvard Law School

openQuestions: The 1889 Act and its cession are recorded under cession-1889-03-02-sioux; this row is the reservation kept. No finding about the Pine Ridge reservation's own land or funds under the 1889 Act was found.
ICC Docket 117 (Pine Ridge accounting, 1971 to 1975 orders) was seen in the index but not read; it may hold a finding.
Later reductions of Pine Ridge by Acts of Congress (after Royce) are not researched here.
